calls.reason: Shumailov et al. show growing repetition across recursive generations, but nobody measured a shift to bland business-speak, and Kazdan et al. find that keeping data mitigates collapse.
Media Matters and the Stanford study document high-reach AI spam examples, but no comparison shows volume beating quality, and the study only suspects the engagement mechanism.
The Hivemind study finds cross-model similarity but leaves the cause open. A 2026 reanalysis disputes the evidence, and alignment research offers another explanation.
TruthfulQA shows models mimicking misconceptions and GPT-4 uses next-token training, but nothing traces errors to stolen data. Adobe's licensed sourcing undercuts the blanket claim.
Google AI summaries grew from 7 to 229 countries and over a billion users. Pew finds people click external links far less when a summary appears, so search access is clearly more AI-mediated.
Google did deploy AI Overviews, but its stated reason was convenience, and its documented response to low-quality content was ranking and spam-policy changes. The causal part is unshown.
